name: Inner Speech Decoding — V4
notes: V4, built 2026-11-02 from the Inner Speech preliminary doc (Aims, Pitfalls, Procedure, Standard and Control Questions tabs). Hard limit: 100 scanner hours; session counts leave about 8% in reserve. Session 1 (consent, training, answering the full bank for ground truth) is outside the scanner and not counted. Design rules: one answer cue (large cross) for every condition so the cue carries no label; yes/no balanced within each standard category (one trial type per category); controls separate answer from question (opposite, no prompt yes/no, neutral "ready", read only, ambiguous); jittered prompt-to-cue delay; item and columns logged with every trial for item-held-out validation.

lists.name: Questions
lists.notes: V4 bank: 40 items per standard category (General Knowledge, Arithmetic, Rhyme Judgment and Category are 20 yes / 20 no; arithmetic answers are computed), 40 Biographical and 40 Emotional with answers recorded per participant (Biographical in the training session, Emotional at each session's debrief), and 30 Ambiguous. Item id and every column are logged with each trial, so analyses can hold items out.

runs.name: Aim 1 — Block localizer

layers.text: When a word appears, repeat it silently at a constant pace for as long as the large cross is shown.

runs.name: Aim 1 — Blocked questions
runs.notes: Affirmative answers first, then negative, then the neutral and read-only controls, with rests between blocks (Aim 1 approach).

layers.text:
When the answer cue (cross) appears and for the entire duration it is shown, answer clearly and silently in your internal voice with a constant pacing of either "yes, yes, yes …" or "no, no, no …".

"Answer: ready" – repeat "ready".   "Answer: the opposite" – repeat the opposite answer.
"Read only – no answer" – just read, no inner speech.   "1 = yes  2 = no" – press the button.

runs.name: Aim 2 — Question run
runs.notes: Event-related single-trial run for LSS betas: each third has one trial of every standard category plus controls; 31 trials.
